function_question: How does nature protect against impact?

opening.text: There was a boy called Kai who helped out at a wildlife rescue centre, caring for hurt and orphaned animals.
Kai checked on a precious egg in the warm incubator, waiting for the day it would hatch.
The egg had to travel to another rescue centre. "The parcel will be bumped and dropped," Kai worried. "How do we keep it safe?"

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Kai must send a precious egg to another rescue centre, and the parcel could fall 2 metres. Can you help him protect it? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some engineers already have a spark of an idea for protecting something fragile. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature has been cushioning bumps for millions of years. Tap each card to meet four heroes who never break!
guide.design_secret: Here's the secret all four heroes share…
guide.skill: Scientists predict before they test. Which wrap will keep the egg safe from 30 cm? Always drop over a tray with an adult nearby.
guide.sketch: Time to draw your packaging cut in half, like a real engineer!
guide.build_and_test: Build your packaging and drop it from 50 cm, then 1 metre, then 2 metres, over a tray or outside. What's the highest drop your egg survives?
guide.retry_tip: Engineers never stop at round 1. Remove ONE layer and test again. Is the egg still safe?
guide.ending: And ever since then, the rescue centre sends every precious egg in packaging like YOURS, and the new chick is growing strong!

quick_check.question: Kai drops the parcel from 50 cm, then 1 metre, then 2 metres. How many centimetres is 2 metres?
quick_check.right: Right! 1 metre is 100 cm, so 2 metres is 200 cm. That's four times higher than the first drop!
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. Remember: 1 metre is 100 centimetres.

clue_cards.name: Woodpecker
clue_cards.trick: A spongy skull bone, with a long tongue bone wrapped around its head.
clue_cards.does: They soak up the shock as it hammers trees up to 20 times a second.

clue_cards.name: Pomelo
clue_cards.trick: Its thick peel is a foam full of air pockets.
clue_cards.does: The pockets squash and spread the impact, so it can fall 10 metres without splitting.

clue_cards.name: Hedgehog
clue_cards.trick: It rolls into a ball covered in springy spines.
clue_cards.does: The spines bend and absorb the shock of landing.

clue_cards.name: Bighorn sheep
clue_cards.trick: Its horns and skull are built in layers.
clue_cards.does: The layers absorb the force when two rams crash heads.

predict.prompt: Sudden stop or slow stop? Predict first!
predict.explain: A fall hurts because things stop suddenly. When something squashes slowly, the stop takes longer and the force is much smaller.

lab.title: The egg drop lab
lab.predict: Drop each egg from 30 cm onto a tray. Which wrap will keep it safest?
